To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 13, New York City Council; Bronx Community Board 11
Subject: Request for safety study at Allerton Avenue & Holland Avenue

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We write to ask NYC DOT to carry out a safety study at the junction of Allerton Avenue & Holland Avenue and to consider fixes on the roads it is responsible for (Allerton Avenue and Holland Avenue).

The official record for the 5 years from 2 November 2021 shows 47 crashes, of which 22 involved injury. Three people were killed. Thirteen pedestrians and 2 cyclists were injured. Using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the harm is valued at $1.5 million per year. The record lists a Leading Pedestrian Interval signal installed in 2025.

We ask you to consider:

- reflective backplates on the traffic signals, which the federal Crash Modification Factors Clearinghouse associates with fewer injury crashes. This would require a site check for an entry on yellow or red. On this basis it is estimated to avoid about 0.7 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $226,000 in harm per year.

- longer yellow signal times, which the Clearinghouse associates with fewer injury crashes. This would require a site check for an entry on yellow or red and whether the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice. On this basis it is estimated to avoid about 0.3 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $118,000 in harm per year.

Please let us know the outcome of the study and any steps planned.

Yours sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

To: the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency (SFMTA)
Cc: your city council member
Subject: Request for safety study at Anza Street & Arguello Boulevard

Dear colleagues at SFMTA,

We write to ask for a safety study for the roads you own at Anza Street & Arguello Boulevard and for fixes that fit what is found on site.

The official record for the 5 years from 2 November 2021 shows 5 crashes and 5 injury crashes. No one was killed. In the U.S. DOT's official values (2024 dollars) the harm is about $0.3 million per year. One safety project is on file for this junction from outside this period: a continental crosswalk in 2016.

This corner got continental crosswalks in 2016. Across the city the earlier program's effect was not shown and repeating it here is not supported by the city's own record.

Please consider, for the roads you own:

* reflective backplates on the traffic signals (Backplates with Retroreflective Borders), expected to prevent about 0.2 injury crashes per year (about $51,000 in harm avoided per year; pays for itself if done for under $0.4 million). This needs a site check for an entry on yellow or red.

* longer yellow signal times (Yellow Change Intervals), expected to prevent about 0.1 injury crashes per year (about $27,000 in harm avoided per year; pays for itself if done for under $0.2 million). This needs a site check for an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.

Thank you for considering a study and for action on the approaches you own.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
